answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by requiring each identity to lock a refundable stake before it may transact. Creating one identity is cheap, but spawning thousands becomes prohibitively expensive, like trying to buy an entire reef one coral at a time. Good behavior earns the stake back with interest, while fraud triggers slashing, so one bad actor cannot spread saffron across a thousand fake stalls. That cost ripple deters mass forgery while honest newcomers still join with a modest deposit.
